text: Every GROUP BY so far has given you one row per group, and nothing more. A real report usually needs more than that — the detail rows, plus a subtotal for each broader category, plus one grand total at the bottom. ROLLUP adds exactly those extra rows, automatically, in a single query.

Color, size, sum of list price, count star, group by rollup, color, size. You still get every color-size detail row from before — but now you also get one subtotal row per color, with size shown as NULL, and one final grand total row, with both color and size NULL.

Here's the part that trips people up: ROLLUP rolls up right to left, strictly in the order you list the columns — not because it understands your data. ROLLUP of color, size subtotals by color first. Flip the order to ROLLUP of size, color, and it subtotals by size instead. SQL Server has no idea which column is really the broader one.

And here's the real problem: Production dot Product has real products where color is genuinely NULL in the data — it's not standing in for anything. Once ROLLUP is also inserting its own NULLs to mean 'this is a subtotal,' a NULL alone can't tell you which situation you're looking at.

That's what GROUPING exists for. Grouping of color returns 1 specifically when that NULL came from ROLLUP, and 0 for any real group value, including a genuine NULL from the data itself. Read the grouping columns together and you can always tell a subtotal row from real data.
Next lesson: GROUP BY CUBE, for when your columns aren't a hierarchy at all, and you want every combination instead of just one roll-up direction.
